correctness.rationale: Exact telegraph two-state generator gives G(t), an instantaneous x-pulse converts pre-pulse y-coherence into conserved z, and conditional transverse decay leaves only z at long time. Gaussian characteristic filtering with a uniform Lipschitz envelope bound gives the blind e^{-s^2/2} factor; phase alignment near the strict maximal slow envelope gives matching lower bounds. Absolute Gaussian cosine convolution and its uniformly convergent Fourier series give the informed b(s), b(infinity)=2/pi, and strict advantage. Uniform fixed-width integration-by-parts provides the independent nonvanishing informed plateau. Numerical standalone 559 checks passed, but analytic proof carries infinite statements.

value.rationale: The strong-telegraph limit forces the optimal pulse time onto increasingly narrow coherence revivals. The exact Gaussian crossover quantifies a physically natural clock-resolution threshold sigma~1/nu, and the observed-time sign feedback yields a sharply different nonzero 2/pi asymptotic capacity despite blind dephasing to zero. This complete, naturally motivated control-information frontier is more than renaming a standard Gaussian identity and yields a falsifiable design and robustness bound. Hardware bandwidth and device energy costs remain outside scope.
